caption_reviews.caption_text: Personnel shows a member’s roles separately from staffing,
status, and administrative state.
In our fictional Chicago Fire department, Casey begins with Officer,
On Shift, Standing By, and Admin.
Choose Manage Roles to inspect the catalog.
The page lists each role’s description and member count.
It also explains how role order chooses an available custom
icon for a person’s map pin.
We will leave the original six roles and their order unchanged, and add one
clearly marked coordination exercise.
Choose Add Role.
Enter Training Only, Community Response Navigator as the Name.
Use the Description to explain the fictional community paramedicine and
mental health coordination exercise.
Our description explicitly separates software training from
professional qualification and system administration privileges.
Custom icon is optional and remains empty.
A useful role name tells another administrator what the role is for;
its description explains the intended scope before anyone is assigned to it.
The lower form previews the default icon on light and dark
backgrounds and in a list.
No custom file has been selected.
Use Save, then
find the new role at the end of the catalog.
Users In Role is zero, and the original six rows retain their order and counts.
Choose View on the new row to read its
stored name and full description.
Creating the role has given us a saved definition, but
has not yet assigned a member.
From the new role’s row, open Required certifications.
The notice says enforcement is Off, and Member eligibility
says the role has no members.
Add requirement creates a row.
Select the fictional record-review type, check Mandatory, leave Any-of
group blank, leave Allow trainee clear, and enter seven for Grace override.
Save, then
reopen the page and read the same single row.
The seven-day setting concerns the removal grace calculation if
enforcement applies; it does not change a certification record’s expiry.
Choose Certification types to verify the full identity behind
the narrow requirement selector.
The training review row shows its complete code, one existing
record, and now one requirement.
Open its Edit control.
Code is read-only, and the help explains that a role
requirement references this type.
Applies to remains locked at Person because a record already uses it.
We are inspecting these fields only.
Keep the existing record and type settings intact.
Back on the role’s requirements page, add a second, distinct
type for an unsaved comparison.
With both Mandatory boxes checked and both group fields
blank, the rows express separate requirements: both would be needed.
Give both rows group number one, and they become alternatives:
either could satisfy that group.
This is a form preview, so do not Save.
Reloading restores the original single row, blank group, and seven-day override.
Saving would replace the stored requirement set; the discarded
preview changes none of it.
To assign the role, return to Personnel and use Edit on Casey’s row.
In the profile’s Roles field, wait for the existing Officer selection to load.
It must remain selected when adding another role.
Group is Truck 81 and Is Group Admin is already checked in this fictional
account; leave both unchanged.
This page contains other profile settings, so keep the exercise
focused on the intended additional role rather than changing membership,
contact, or administrative options.
Use the profile’s Roles selector for the additional assignment.
Community is entered in the lookup, while Officer remains selected.
The prepared selection then contains two complete chips:
Officer and the new Training Only, Community Response Navigator role.
Read both names before saving.
This control submits the whole selected role set, so an existing role must remain
present if you intend to preserve it.
Adding the new chip is preparation; we still need a saved readback.
Before saving, compare the unchanged profile controls.
Department Admin is already selected, while Disable User
and Hide User are clear. We leave them that way.
Use the normal Save once.
Back in Personnel, search for Matthew Casey.
His row now lists Officer and the new coordination role together.
Staffing remains On Shift, status remains Standing By, and
administrative state still reads Admin.
The result is an additional operational role on the same member, not a
new staffing or status selection.
Use the member’s Edit control again to check persistence.
Both role chips are present in the fresh profile.
Truck 81 remains selected and Is Group Admin remains checked.
Farther down, Department Admin is still selected, while Disable
User and Hide User remain clear.
This second visit is read-only.
Verify the particular fields involved in your exercise instead of assuming that
a typed or selected value was stored.
Keep unrelated profile and permission choices unchanged.
Return through Manage Roles.
The new role now has one member.
Choose its View control to see
Casey listed under the stored description.
Open Required certifications from that role’s
row to inspect Member eligibility.
Casey is marked Qualified for this single fictional software rule.
The Off notice remains visible: this result does not demonstrate
enforcement blocking or removal.
Read the rule, the member, and the software result together, and keep
professional authorization decisions outside this training exercise.
Chicago Fire can use this workflow to describe an exercise coordination role.
Community care and mental health teams can organize operational
responsibilities without patient detail.
Search and rescue can distinguish search and support roles; security
teams can define site responsibilities; wildland teams can organize seasonal
coordination; and industrial response teams can separate staff
functions from equipment inspections.
In each setting, use clear descriptions, deliberate
requirements, and verified membership.
Preserve existing assignments and administrative settings, and check
saved results before relying on them.

limits: Whole-second service markers do not provide millisecond word precision.
Raw75 and76 adjacent unchanged words share source022 and use their measured outer boundaries.
Casey caption holds through an actual recorded gap to the next raw cue; no estimated speech boundary.
The selected requirement type truncates; fullidentity is independently pictured in the type catalog and locked Code view.
The role-search option is clipped; only the typed Community query and retained Officer chip are claimed there. Both complete chips follow.
Two-row AND/OR forms are unsaved previews. Fresh reload restores the single saved rule.
Qualified is the software result for one fictional rule while enforcement remains Off, without blocking or removal proof.
No change to existing staffing, status, group administration or department administration is demonstrated.
No upload, provider delivery, clinical or professional authorization proof.
